reason: The text describes a confrontational scenario during the plagues of Egypt where Moses and Aaron execute God's commands against Pharaoh and Egypt. Rather than depicting collaboration, the passage shows Pharaoh repeatedly refusing to heed Moses and Aaron's demands ("לֹא־ יִשְׁמַע אֲלֵיכֶם פַּרְעֹה" - Pharaoh will not listen/obey you). The Egyptian people are portrayed as victims suffering from the plagues (frogs, hail, locusts, darkness) alongside their livestock and crops, not as willing collaborators. While Moses and Aaron do work together as a team, they are not collaborating with the people—rather, they are instruments of divine judgment against those people. Pharaoh's repeated hardening of heart and refusal to release the Israelites further contradicts any notion of cooperative leadership.
